career_paths.title: Android Developer
career_paths.description: Master modern Android development with Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, and Clean Architecture.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Variables: val vs var
knowledge_nuggets.content: In Kotlin, 'val' creates a read-only (immutable) variable, meaning its value cannot be changed once assigned. 'var' creates a mutable variable. Best practice is to use 'val' by default to make your code safer and more predictable.

quizzes.text: Which keyword should you use to declare a variable whose value will NEVER change?
quizzes.explanation: 'val' stands for value and creates an immutable reference.

quizzes.text: What happens if you try to reassign a value to a 'val' variable?
quizzes.explanation: Since 'val' is immutable, the compiler will not allow you to reassign it.

knowledge_nuggets.title: String Templates
knowledge_nuggets.content: Kotlin allows embedding variables and expressions directly into string literals using the $ symbol. For example: "Hello $name! 2+2 is ${2+2}".

quizzes.text: How do you evaluate an expression inside a String template?
quizzes.explanation: Use curly braces ${} to evaluate complex expressions inside a string.

knowledge_nuggets.title: The 'when' Expression
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Kotlin's powerful replacement for switch statements.
knowledge_nuggets.content: 'when' replaces the C-style switch statement. It is an expression, meaning it returns a value. It supports complex matching like checking types (is String), ranges (in 1..10), and doesn't require a 'break' statement.

quizzes.text: Does a 'when' expression in Kotlin require a 'break' statement at the end of each branch?
quizzes.explanation: No, Kotlin's 'when' automatically stops execution after a matching branch is found. No 'break' is needed.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Null Safety
knowledge_nuggets.content: Kotlin distinguishes between nullable types (String?) and non-nullable types (String). Use the safe call operator (?.) to call methods on nullable objects, and the Elvis operator (?:) to provide a default value if an object is null.

quizzes.text: What will 'val length = name?.length ?: 0' return if 'name' is null?
quizzes.explanation: The Elvis operator (?:) returns the right side (0) because the left side resulted in null.

quizzes.text: What does the !! (Not-null assertion) operator do?
options: Throws an NPE if the value is null
quizzes.explanation: !! forces the compiler to treat the value as non-null, throwing an exception if it actually is null. Avoid using it!

knowledge_nuggets.title: Singleton Pattern with 'object'
knowledge_nuggets.content: In Java, implementing the Singleton pattern requires boilerplate code (private constructor, static instance, thread-safety). In Kotlin, simply declaring 'object MySingleton' handles all of this automatically under the hood.

quizzes.text: Which keyword is used in Kotlin to declare a Singleton?
quizzes.explanation: The 'object' declaration creates a class and an instance of that class at the same time, perfectly implementing the Singleton pattern safely.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Companion Objects
knowledge_nuggets.content: Kotlin does not have 'static' keywords. Instead, you can define a 'companion object' inside a class to hold methods and properties that are tied to the class rather than instances.

quizzes.text: What replaces static methods in Kotlin?
quizzes.explanation: Companion objects allow you to call functions using the class name, similar to static methods in Java.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Activity Lifecycle
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Understand how Activities are created and destroyed.
knowledge_nuggets.content: The Activity lifecycle consists of states like onCreate, onStart, onResume, onPause, onStop, and onDestroy. Managing these correctly prevents memory leaks and ensures a smooth user experience when switching apps.

quizzes.text: Which method is called first when an Activity is created?
quizzes.explanation: onCreate() is the first callback and where you initialize your activity.

quizzes.text: Which state is an Activity in when it is partially obscured but still visible?
quizzes.explanation: onPause() is called when the activity is no longer in the foreground but still visible.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Compose State
knowledge_nuggets.content: In Compose, state is any value that can change over time. When state updates, Compose automatically re-executes the functions (recomposition) to reflect the changes in the UI.

quizzes.text: Which function is used to keep state across recompositions?
quizzes.explanation: remember stores an object in the composition.

knowledge_nuggets.title: ViewModel Pattern
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Manage UI data in a lifecycle-aware way.
knowledge_nuggets.content: ViewModels store and manage UI-related data so it survives configuration changes like screen rotations. They decouple your UI logic from the Activity/Fragment lifecycle.

quizzes.text: Does a ViewModel survive a screen rotation?
quizzes.explanation: Yes, ViewModels are specifically designed to survive configuration changes.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Jetpack Navigation
knowledge_nuggets.content: The Navigation component helps you implement navigation, from simple button clicks to complex patterns, such as app bars and the navigation drawer.

quizzes.text: What is the new recommended way to define routes in Navigation 2.8.0+?
quizzes.explanation: Navigation now supports type-safe routes using Kotlin Serialization.

knowledge_nuggets.title: DataStore
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: The modern way to store preferences.
knowledge_nuggets.content: DataStore is a data storage solution that allows you to store key-value pairs or typed objects with protocol buffers. It uses Coroutines and Flow to store data asynchronously.

quizzes.text: What does DataStore replace?
quizzes.explanation: DataStore is the replacement for SharedPreferences.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Data Classes
knowledge_nuggets.content: Adding the 'data' keyword to a class automatically generates equals(), hashCode(), toString(), componentN() functions, and a copy() function. It is perfect for DTOs and holding state in modern architectures.

quizzes.text: Which built-in function allows you to duplicate a Data Class object while modifying specific properties?
quizzes.explanation: The copy() function lets you copy an object, altering some of its properties while keeping the rest unchanged.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Extension Functions
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Add functionality to classes without inheriting.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Extension functions allow you to add new functions to an existing class (even from third-party libraries) without modifying its source code. Example: fun String.removeSpaces() = this.replace(" ", "")

quizzes.text: Can extension functions access private variables or methods of the class they are extending?
options: Only if placed in the same file
quizzes.explanation: Extension functions are resolved statically and do not truly modify the class, so they cannot access private members.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Lateinit vs Lazy
knowledge_nuggets.content: 'lateinit var' is used for variables that will be initialized later (e.g., in Android onCreate). 'val x by lazy' computes its value only upon first access and remembers it.

quizzes.text: Which initialization delegate is thread-safe by default?
quizzes.explanation: 'lazy' is synchronized and thread-safe by default.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Higher-Order Functions & Lambdas
knowledge_nuggets.content: A higher-order function is a function that takes another function as a parameter or returns one. Lambdas are anonymous functions. If a lambda is the last parameter of a function, you can place it outside the parentheses (Trailing Lambda).

quizzes.text: In a lambda with a single parameter, what is the implicit name of that parameter?
quizzes.explanation: If a lambda has only one parameter, Kotlin implicitly names it 'it' to keep the code concise.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Collections & Transformations
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Master map, filter, and functional APIs.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Kotlin standard library offers powerful list operations. Use 'map' to transform every item, 'filter' to remove items matching a condition, and 'flatten' to combine nested lists into one.

quizzes.text: Which functional operator would you use to transform a List<User> into a List<String> containing only their names?
quizzes.explanation: 'map' applies a transformation function to each element and returns a new list of the results.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Kotlin Coroutines
knowledge_nuggets.content: Coroutines allow you to write asynchronous code as if it were synchronous. They are highly efficient and provide built-in cancellation and structured concurrency.

quizzes.text: What keyword is used to define a coroutine-friendly function?
quizzes.explanation: suspend functions can be paused and resumed without blocking.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Kotlin Flow
knowledge_nuggets.content: Flow is a stream of data that can be computed asynchronously. It is similar to an Iterator but uses suspend functions for asynchronous values.

quizzes.text: Which Flow type is best for representing UI state?
quizzes.explanation: StateFlow is a state-holder observable flow that emits the current and new state updates.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Room Database
knowledge_nuggets.content: Room provides an abstraction layer over SQLite to allow fluent database access while harnessing the full power of SQLite. It handles boilerplate and provides compile-time checks.

quizzes.text: What does a DAO stand for in Room?
quizzes.explanation: DAOs define the methods that access the database.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Retrofit Networking
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Connect your app to the internet.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Retrofit is a type-safe HTTP client for Android. it turns your HTTP API into a Java/Kotlin interface, making network requests easy to handle and test.

quizzes.text: Which library is often used with Retrofit for JSON parsing?
quizzes.explanation: Converter factories like Gson or Kotlinx Serialization handle JSON mapping.

knowledge_nuggets.title: WorkManager
knowledge_nuggets.content: WorkManager is the recommended solution for persistent work. It handles tasks that need to run even if the app exits or the device restarts, like data syncing.

quizzes.text: Is WorkManager suitable for immediate, high-priority tasks?
options: Only if the app is open
quizzes.explanation: WorkManager is for tasks that can wait but must eventually run.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Hilt Dependency Injection
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Standardize DI in your Android apps.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Hilt is a DI library for Android that reduces the boilerplate of manual dependency injection. It is built on top of Dagger and provides a standard way to incorporate DI into your app.

quizzes.text: Which annotation is used to mark the Application class for Hilt?
quizzes.explanation: @HiltAndroidApp triggers Hilt's code generation.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Solid Principles - SRP
knowledge_nuggets.content: A class should have only one reason to change. This means a class should only perform one primary task, making it easier to maintain and test.

quizzes.text: What happens if you violate SRP?
quizzes.explanation: Violating SRP leads to massive classes that are hard to debug.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Testing - JUnit
knowledge_nuggets.content: JUnit is the standard testing framework for Android. Unit tests verify the smallest parts of your app in isolation, usually the business logic in your Domain or ViewModels.

quizzes.text: Where do unit tests usually reside in the project structure?
quizzes.explanation: Local unit tests run on the JVM and go into the 'test' folder.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Smart Casts
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Let the compiler do the casting.
knowledge_nuggets.content: If you check the type of an object using the 'is' keyword, the Kotlin compiler automatically tracks this and casts the variable to the target type within the checked scope.

quizzes.text: Which operator is used to check if an object is of a certain type?
quizzes.explanation: The 'is' operator checks the type, and smart casting automatically applies it.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Scope Functions (let, apply, run...)
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Execute code within the context of an object.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Kotlin provides 5 scope functions: let, run, with, apply, and also. 'apply' is used for object configuration (returns the object). 'let' is great for executing a block only if the object is non-null (returns the lambda result).

quizzes.text: Which scope function is best suited for configuring an object (e.g., setting UI properties) and returns the object itself ('this')?
quizzes.explanation: 'apply' refers to the context object as 'this' and returns the object itself, making it perfect for initialization.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Sealed Classes & Interfaces
knowledge_nuggets.content: Sealed classes restrict inheritance. All subclasses must be known at compile-time (declared in the same package/file). They are extensively used in Android to represent UI States (e.g., Loading, Success, Error).

quizzes.text: When using a Sealed Class in a 'when' expression to handle all possible subclasses, do you need an 'else' branch?
options: No, the compiler knows all subclasses
Only if there are more than 3 subclasses
quizzes.explanation: Because sealed class hierarchies are strictly bounded, the compiler can verify that you have covered all possible cases, making the 'else' branch unnecessary.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Inline Functions
knowledge_nuggets.content: Using 'inline' tells the compiler to copy the function's bytecode directly into the call site. This eliminates the memory overhead of creating lambda objects in higher-order functions.

quizzes.text: What is the main benefit of using the 'inline' keyword?
quizzes.explanation: Inlining prevents object allocation for lambdas, improving performance.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Clean Architecture
knowledge_nuggets.content: Clean Architecture divides the app into layers (Data, Domain, Presentation). The Domain layer contains business logic and is independent of UI or external libraries.

quizzes.text: Which layer should NOT know about Android frameworks?
quizzes.explanation: The Domain layer should be pure Kotlin/Java with no dependencies on the platform.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Advanced R8/Proguard
knowledge_nuggets.content: R8 is the built-in tool that shrinks, desugars, and obfuscates your code. Obfuscation renames classes and members to make reverse engineering more difficult.

quizzes.text: What is the primary goal of obfuscation?
options: Make code harder to read for humans
quizzes.explanation: Obfuscation protects intellectual property by making reverse engineering difficult.

career_paths.title: UI/UX Designer
career_paths.description: Learn to design beautiful, user-centered mobile and web applications.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Color Theory
knowledge_nuggets.content: Color theory involves the color wheel, harmony, and the psychological impact of colors. Warm colors evoke energy, while cool colors suggest calmness.

quizzes.text: Which color is often associated with trust and professionalism?
quizzes.explanation: Blue is widely used in corporate and financial apps to build trust.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Grid Systems
knowledge_nuggets.content: Grids provide structure and consistency. A standard 8dp or 4dp grid helps in aligning elements and ensures that the layout looks professional across all screens.

quizzes.text: Why use an 8dp grid system?
options: Consistency and divisible by most screen sizes
quizzes.explanation: An 8dp grid makes scaling across different screen densities easier.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Wireframing
knowledge_nuggets.content: Wireframes are low-fidelity sketches that focus on layout and functionality without getting distracted by colors or typography. They are the 'skeleton' of your UI.

quizzes.text: What is the main purpose of a wireframe?
quizzes.explanation: Wireframes define where elements go and how the user moves between screens.

knowledge_nuggets.title: User Research
knowledge_nuggets.content: User research involves interviews, surveys, and testing to understand user needs. Designing without research is like shooting in the dark.

quizzes.text: What is a 'User Persona'?
options: A fictional character representing a user segment
quizzes.explanation: Personas help teams empathize with the target audience.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Accessibility (A11y)
knowledge_nuggets.content: Accessibility ensures that people with disabilities can use your app. This includes screen reader support, large touch targets, and high contrast ratios.

quizzes.text: What is the minimum recommended touch target size?
quizzes.explanation: 48x48dp is the minimum size for comfortable tapping.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Contrast Ratio
knowledge_nuggets.content: The contrast ratio measures the difference in brightness between text and background. WCAG 2.1 requires at least 4.5:1 for normal text.

quizzes.text: Which ratio is better for accessibility?
quizzes.explanation: Higher contrast makes text easier to read for users with low vision.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Visual Hierarchy
knowledge_nuggets.content: Visual hierarchy uses size, color, and weight to show importance. It helps users scan a page quickly and find the information they need.

quizzes.text: How do you create visual hierarchy?
quizzes.explanation: Contrast in size and weight tells the user what to read first.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Fitts's Law
knowledge_nuggets.content: Fitts's Law states that the time to move to a target depends on the target's size and distance. In UI, place frequently used buttons close and make them large.

quizzes.text: According to Fitts's Law, what makes a target easier to hit?
quizzes.explanation: Large, nearby buttons are fastest to interact with.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Micro-interactions
knowledge_nuggets.content: Micro-interactions are subtle animations that confirm a user's action. Example: A heart icon that pops when liked or a loading bar that moves.

quizzes.text: What do micro-interactions provide?
quizzes.explanation: They make the app feel responsive and human-centric.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Design Systems
knowledge_nuggets.content: A design system is a collection of reusable components, guided by clear standards, that can be assembled together to build any number of applications.

quizzes.text: What is the main benefit of a design system?
quizzes.explanation: It ensures consistency and speed across large products.

career_paths.title: IELTS Academic Prep
career_paths.description: Master Listening, Reading, Writing, and Speaking strategies to achieve Band 7.5+ for your study abroad journey.

knowledge_nuggets.title: IELTS Academic Format
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Understand the 4 modules and band scoring.
knowledge_nuggets.content: IELTS Academic tests 4 skills: Listening (30 mins), Reading (60 mins), Writing (60 mins), and Speaking (11-14 mins). Each module is scored from Band 0 to 9, and your overall score is rounded to the nearest 0.5 or whole band (e.g., 6.25 becomes 6.5, while 6.125 becomes 6.0).

quizzes.text: If your average score across all four modules is 6.75, what will your final Overall Band Score be?
quizzes.explanation: In IELTS, an average ending in .75 is always rounded up to the next whole band (7.0).

quizzes.text: How much total time is given for the IELTS Reading module?
quizzes.explanation: You get exactly 60 minutes to answer 40 questions across 3 passages, with no extra time to transfer answers.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Listening: Distractors
knowledge_nuggets.content: A very common trap in IELTS Listening is the 'distractor'—where a speaker gives a piece of information and then corrects themselves (e.g., 'Let's meet on Tuesday... oh wait, I have a class, let's make it Thursday'). Always wait for the speaker to finish the sentence before locking in your answer.

quizzes.text: Speaker: 'The postcode isSW1 4BT... sorry, my mistake, it's SW1 4BP.' What is the correct answer?
quizzes.explanation: The first postcode is a distractor. Words like 'sorry', 'however', or 'actually' signal a correction.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Listening: Word Limit Rules
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Never lose marks over instruction rules.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Always read instructions like 'NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER'. If the instruction says 'ONE WORD ONLY' and you write 'a hospital' instead of 'hospital', your answer will be marked completely wrong even though you heard the right word.

quizzes.text: Instruction: 'NO MORE THAN ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER'. Which answer is valid?
quizzes.explanation: '25 buses' consists of one number (25) and one word (buses), fitting the exact instruction.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Reading: Skimming & Scanning
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Read faster without reading every word.
knowledge_nuggets.content: You do not have time to read all 3 passages word-for-word. Use 'Skimming' (reading titles, headings, and first sentences rapidly) to get the main idea. Use 'Scanning' to hunt for specific keywords like names, dates, numbers, and technical terms.

quizzes.text: What is the best technique to quickly find a scientist's name (e.g., 'Dr. Smith') in a long passage?
quizzes.explanation: Scanning helps you locate specific nouns, capital letters, and numbers without reading full sentences.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Speaking Part 1: The A-R-E Method
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Avoid one-word answers in the interview.
knowledge_nuggets.content: In Speaking Part 1, the examiner asks familiar questions about your home, studies, or hobbies. Never reply with just 'Yes' or 'No'. Use the A-R-E method: Answer the question directly, give a Reason, and provide a short Example (aim for 2 to 3 natural sentences).

quizzes.text: How long should a typical response be in Speaking Part 1?
quizzes.explanation: 2 to 3 well-connected sentences show fluency without rambling.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Reading: True, False, Not Given
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Master the trickiest Reading question type.
knowledge_nuggets.content: TRUE means the passage proves the statement. FALSE means the passage directly contradicts (says the opposite of) the statement. NOT GIVEN means the specific information is simply not mentioned—never use your own outside knowledge to assume an answer!

quizzes.text: Passage: 'Most students prefer digital textbooks.' Statement: 'All students prefer digital textbooks.' What is the answer?
quizzes.explanation: 'Most' directly contradicts 'All'. Watch out for extreme qualifiers like all, always, never, and only.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Reading: Matching Headings
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Identify the main theme of paragraphs.
knowledge_nuggets.content: When matching headings to paragraphs, always read the paragraph's first two sentences and last sentence first, as they usually contain the topic sentence. Beware of headings that just repeat a minor detail or example from the middle of the paragraph.

quizzes.text: What does a correct heading represent?
options: A specific date in the paragraph
The central idea of the whole paragraph
The last word of the paragraph
quizzes.explanation: Headings summarize the main purpose of the entire paragraph, not a single detail.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Writing Task 1: The Overview
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: The most important paragraph in Task 1.
knowledge_nuggets.content: In Academic Writing Task 1 (150+ words, 20 mins), you summarize a chart, graph, map, or process. To score Band 7+ in Task Achievement, you MUST include a clear 'Overview' paragraph highlighting 2-3 main trends (highest/lowest points or overall changes) without mentioning specific numbers.

quizzes.text: What should you AVOID putting inside your Task 1 Overview paragraph?
options: Specific percentages and raw data numbers
quizzes.explanation: Save specific data and numbers for the Body Paragraphs; the Overview is only for big-picture trends.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Writing Task 1: Vocabulary of Trends
knowledge_nuggets.content: Avoid repeating basic words like 'went up' or 'went down'. Use precise verbs and adverbs: 'rose dramatically', 'plummeted', 'fluctuated wildly', 'remained stable', or 'peaked at'. Never give personal opinions or reasons not shown in the chart.

quizzes.text: Which word best describes a sudden, very large drop in a line graph?
quizzes.explanation: 'Plummeted' means fell or dropped straight down at high speed.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Speaking Part 2: The Cue Card
knowledge_nuggets.content: In Part 2, you get 1 minute to prepare and must speak for 1-2 minutes on a given topic. If you run out of things to say, use the Past-Present-Future (PPF) strategy: briefly mention your past experience with the topic, describe the present situation, and share future hopes related to it.

quizzes.text: How much preparation time do you get before speaking in Part 2?
quizzes.explanation: You are given pencil, paper, and exactly 1 minute to jot down keyword notes.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Writing Task 2: Essay Structure
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Plan your 250-word essay for high bands.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Task 2 carries 66% of your total Writing score (40 mins, 250+ words). Use a proven 4-paragraph structure: 1) Introduction (Paraphrase prompt + clear Thesis/Opinion), 2) Body Paragraph 1 (Main idea + explanation + specific example), 3) Body Paragraph 2, and 4) Conclusion (Summarize main points).

quizzes.text: Which Writing task carries more weight in your final Writing Band score?
options: Task 2 (worth twice as much as Task 1)
quizzes.explanation: Task 2 accounts for two-thirds of your writing grade, so manage your time wisely!

knowledge_nuggets.title: Coherence & Cohesion
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Connect ideas smoothly without overusing linkers.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Coherence is how logical your ideas are; Cohesion is how sentences connect. Use linking words naturally (However, Furthermore, Consequently, For instance). However, do not start every single sentence with a mechanical linker—use pronouns ('this issue', 'such measures') for natural flow.

quizzes.text: Which linking word is used to introduce a contrasting or opposite idea?
quizzes.explanation: 'Nevertheless' (like 'However') introduces a contrast to the previous statement.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Lexical Resource & Collocations
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Use natural word partnerships instead of memorizing rare words.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Examiners don't want archaic dictionary words; they want 'Collocations'—words that naturally go together in English (e.g., 'heavy rain' instead of 'strong rain', 'play a pivotal role', 'mitigate the problem', 'sedentary lifestyle'). Incorrectly using big words lowers your score.

quizzes.text: Which of the following is a natural academic collocation?
quizzes.explanation: In English, 'make a mistake' is the natural collocation, whereas 'do a mistake' is incorrect.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Grammatical Range & Accuracy
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Boost your score with complex sentence structures.
knowledge_nuggets.content: To hit Band 7+ in Grammar, you must mix simple and complex sentences. Practice using subordinate clauses (Although..., While..., Despite...), relative clauses (which, who, that), and conditionals ('If governments invested more in public transport, traffic congestion would decrease').

quizzes.text: Which sentence is a grammatically correct complex sentence?
options: Although it rained, but we went out.
Although it rained, we went out.
Despite it rained, we went out.
It rained, however we went out.
quizzes.explanation: In English, you never use 'but' after 'Although' in the same sentence.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Speaking Part 3: Abstract Discussion
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Handle deep, analytical questions like a pro.
knowledge_nuggets.content: In Part 3, the examiner asks broad, societal questions (e.g., 'How will technology change education in the future?'). Don't talk about yourself here; talk about people in general. Use 'hedging' phrases to sound academic: 'It is widely believed that...', 'That largely depends on...', or 'In all likelihood...'

quizzes.text: In Speaking Part 3, should your answers focus on your personal life or society in general?
quizzes.explanation: Part 1 & 2 are personal, whereas Part 3 tests your ability to discuss abstract, general, and societal topics.

career_paths.title: CV Interview Masterclass
career_paths.description: Tailored interview preparation based on your CV: Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Barnoi POS, BariPlus, MVVM, Hilt, Room, and React Native.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Self-Intro & Project Pitch
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: How to introduce yourself and highlight Play Store apps.
knowledge_nuggets.content: When asked 'Tell me about yourself', use the Present-Past-Future formula: Start with your current role as an Associate Software Engineer at Softzino Technologies building native Android apps with Kotlin & Compose (like Barnoi POS). Mention your 3+ years of overall tech experience and your published Play Store apps—BariPlus (5K+ downloads, 4.8 rating in React Native) and Bidyava (Kotlin eLearning app). Conclude with why you are excited about this new role.

quizzes.text: What is the most impactful metric from your CV to mention during your introduction?
quizzes.explanation: Production experience with real users and high ratings (BariPlus & Bidyava) immediately proves you can deliver end-to-end products.

knowledge_nuggets.title: StateFlow vs SharedFlow
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: A guaranteed interview question from your Barnoi POS stack.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Both are hot flows. StateFlow requires an initial value, replays the latest value to new collectors, and only emits when the value actually changes (distinctUntilChanged). It holds UI State. SharedFlow has no initial value by default, is highly configurable (replay cache, buffer), and emits even if the value is identical—making it ideal for one-time UI events like navigation, snackbars, or payment failure alerts in Barnoi POS.

quizzes.text: In Barnoi POS, if a payment fails and you want to show a Snackbar ONLY ONCE (not again on screen rotation), which should you use?
quizzes.explanation: SharedFlow (with replay = 0) or a Channel ensures one-time events are not re-triggered upon configuration changes.

quizzes.text: What happens if you emit the exact same value twice in a row to a StateFlow?
quizzes.explanation: StateFlow uses structural equality (.equals()) and conflates identical consecutive values.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Compose Recomposition & Stability
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: How to explain UI performance optimization in Jetpack Compose.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Recomposition is the process of calling your composable functions again when inputs (state) change. To optimize Compose UI: 1) Use State Hoisting to keep composables stateless, 2) Pass immutable data or mark classes with @Immutable / @Stable so Compose can skip unnecessary recompositions, 3) Use 'key' inside LazyColumn (e.g., product list in POS), and 4) Use 'derivedStateOf' when state changes faster than the UI needs to update.

quizzes.text: Why does passing a standard Kotlin 'List<T>' sometimes cause unnecessary recomposition in Compose?
options: Compose compiler sees List interface as unstable because it could be backed by a MutableList
Lists cannot be used in Compose
quizzes.explanation: Because List is an interface that MutableList implements, Compose cannot guarantee immutability without @Immutable wrappers or Kotlinx ImmutableLists.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Compose Side-Effects
knowledge_nuggets.content: A side-effect is any change to the state of the app that happens outside the scope of a composable function. Use 'LaunchedEffect(key)' to run suspend functions safely inside a composable (cancels and restarts if key changes). Use 'DisposableEffect' when cleanup is required (e.g., disconnecting a Bluetooth printer listener or stopping ExoPlayer). Use 'SideEffect' to publish Compose state to non-compose code.

quizzes.text: Which Side-Effect handler is best for registering and unregistering a broadcast receiver or hardware callback?
quizzes.explanation: DisposableEffect provides an 'onDispose' block specifically designed to clean up listeners and prevent memory leaks.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Coroutines: Dispatchers & Scopes
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Explain threading, viewModelScope, and structured concurrency.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Dispatchers determine which thread a coroutine runs on: Dispatchers.Main (UI interactions), Dispatchers.IO (Network, Room DB, File I/O), and Dispatchers.Default (CPU-intensive work like sorting large POS inventories or parsing huge JSONs). 'supervisorScope' ensures that if one child coroutine fails, the sibling coroutines are not cancelled.

quizzes.text: In a ViewModel, if one parallel API call fails inside a supervisorScope, what happens to the other running API call?
quizzes.explanation: Unlike coroutineScope, a supervisorScope does not propagate cancellation from one failing child to its siblings.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Offline-First Architecture & Room
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Defend your Softzino experience on local caching strategies.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Your CV highlights 'offline-first capabilities using Room Database'. In an interview, explain the Single Source of Truth (SSOT) pattern: The UI ONLY observes data from Room Database (via Flow<List<Entity>>). When requesting data, the Repository fetches from the Retrofit API in the background, saves the response into Room inside a transaction, and Room automatically emits the updated data to the UI.

quizzes.text: In a true Offline-First architecture, where does the ViewModel directly read data from?
options: From the Local Database (Single Source of Truth)
quizzes.explanation: The local database acts as the Single Source of Truth; network responses update the database, which then notifies the UI via Flow.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Retrofit, OkHttp & Interceptors
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Explain API caching, auth tokens, and Moshi parsing.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Retrofit uses OkHttp under the hood. In interviews, you will be asked how you handle JWT Auth Tokens and API Caching (mentioned in your CV). Answer: 'I use an OkHttp Interceptor to automatically attach the Bearer token to every request header, and an Authenticator (or refresh token interceptor) to handle 401 Unauthorized responses by refreshing the token seamlessly. For parsing, I prefer Moshi because it supports Kotlin codegen and is faster than reflection-based Gson.'

quizzes.text: Why is Moshi with codegen preferred over Gson in modern Kotlin Android apps?
options: Moshi understands Kotlin null-safety, default values, and avoids slow runtime reflection
Moshi is built into Android OS
quizzes.explanation: Gson is written in Java and ignores Kotlin's non-null types and default parameter values unless specially configured, whereas Moshi is Kotlin-friendly.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Dagger Hilt: @Binds vs @Provides
knowledge_nuggets.content: You use '@Provides' in a Hilt Module when creating an instance of a third-party class (like Retrofit, OkHttp, or RoomDatabase) where you don't own the constructor. You use '@Binds' on an abstract function when you want to tell Hilt which implementation class to use for an Interface (e.g., binding PosRepositoryImpl to PosRepository). '@Binds' generates less code and is more efficient.

quizzes.text: When binding a Repository Interface to its Implementation class in Hilt, which annotation is more efficient?
quizzes.explanation: @Binds is used on abstract methods and generates minimal boilerplate code compared to @Provides.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Barnoi POS: Deep Dive Defense
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: How to answer architecture questions about your POS project.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Interviewers will ask: 'What was the hardest challenge in Barnoi POS?' Great answer: 'Managing complex cart state with multi-payment splits (Cash, Card, MFS, Voucher, Store Credit), discount calculations, and exchanges/refunds without UI lag. I solved this using an immutable UI state in the ViewModel powered by StateFlow, handling barcode scanner inputs asynchronously, and isolating thermal printer ESC/POS byte-stream commands in a dedicated hardware manager.'

quizzes.text: When handling financial calculations (discounts, tax, multi-payments) in a POS app, which data type avoids floating-point precision bugs?
quizzes.explanation: Float and Double suffer from binary floating-point inaccuracy (e.g., 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004). BigDecimal or integer cents ensure exact currency math.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Bidyava: Exam Timer & State
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Defending your eLearning & BCS model test app.
knowledge_nuggets.content: For Bidyava, interviewers often ask: 'How did you handle the live exam countdown timer so it doesn't reset on screen rotation or lag the UI?' Answer: 'I ran the timer inside the ViewModel using Kotlin Coroutines/Flow rather than the UI layer, or calculated remaining time using SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() against the exam end-timestamp. This ensures configuration changes or brief backgrounding never corrupt the remaining exam time.'

quizzes.text: Why is relying purely on 'delay(1000)' in a loop risky for a strict exam countdown timer?
options: Thread scheduling delays and backgrounding can cause time drift; comparing against system timestamps is more accurate
quizzes.explanation: Comparing current elapsed time against a target timestamp prevents cumulative drift if the CPU is busy.

knowledge_nuggets.title: React Native: Architecture & BariPlus
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Key React Native questions for cross-platform roles.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Since BariPlus has 5K+ downloads in React Native, expect questions on RN performance and architecture: 1) Old Bridge vs New Architecture: The old architecture serialized JSON asynchronously over a Bridge, causing bottlenecks. The New Architecture uses JSI (JavaScript Interface) in C++ for synchronous, direct communication between JS and Native modules, plus Fabric (new renderer) and TurboModules. 2) FlatList optimization: Use keyExtractor, getItemLayout, windowSize, and React.memo.

quizzes.text: What replaces the asynchronous JSON Bridge in React Native's New Architecture?
quizzes.explanation: JSI allows JavaScript to hold references to C++ Host Objects and invoke native methods directly and synchronously.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Memory Leaks in Android
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: How leaks happen and how to detect them.
knowledge_nuggets.content: A memory leak happens when the Garbage Collector (GC) cannot free an object because a longer-lived object still holds a reference to it. Common causes: 1) Passing Activity 'Context' to a Singleton, 2) Uncancelled Coroutines or RxJava subscriptions, 3) Unregistered listeners/receivers. Use LeakCanary in debug builds and Android Studio Memory Profiler to detect leaks.

quizzes.text: Why should you never store a reference to a View or Activity Context inside a ViewModel?
options: ViewModel outlives the Activity on rotation, causing a severe memory leak of the entire Activity
quizzes.explanation: Because the ViewModel survives configuration changes, holding an Activity reference prevents the old destroyed Activity from being garbage collected.

knowledge_nuggets.title: MVVM vs MVI Architecture
knowledge_nuggets.content: In MVVM, the View observes multiple streams or a UI state from the ViewModel and calls functions on the ViewModel. In MVI (Model-View-Intent), there is a strict Unidirectional Data Flow (UDF) with a single immutable 'UiState' data class and a single entry point for user actions via sealed classes/interfaces called 'Intents' or 'Events'. Jetpack Compose pairs naturally with MVI/UDF.

quizzes.text: What is the core advantage of having a single immutable UiState object in MVVM/MVI?
options: Eliminates inconsistent or conflicting UI states (Single Source of Truth for the screen)
quizzes.explanation: A single state object guarantees the UI is always rendering a predictable, reproducible snapshot of data.

knowledge_nuggets.title: DSA & Time Complexity (HackerRank)
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Back up your 90+ HackerRank solutions claim.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Since your CV mentions 90+ HackerRank DSA solutions, interviewers will test your Big-O knowledge and basic data structures. Remember: HashMap/HashSet lookup is O(1) average time—always use a HashMap to optimize nested O(n^2) loops down to O(n) (e.g., Two Sum, finding duplicates, frequency counting). Binary Search on a sorted array is O(log n). Sorting an array takes O(n log n).

quizzes.text: How can you reduce an O(n²) nested loop that searches for pairs with a given sum into O(n) time complexity?
options: Use a HashMap / HashSet to store seen complements
quizzes.explanation: Storing visited elements in a HashSet/HashMap allows O(1) complement lookups, bringing total time complexity down to O(n).

knowledge_nuggets.title: Play Store Release, R8 & Signing
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Prove your real-world app publishing expertise.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Having published BariPlus and Bidyava, you may be asked about the release pipeline: 1) Android App Bundle (.aab) vs APK: Play Store uses .aab to generate optimized split APKs for each user's device density/ABI, reducing download size. 2) R8/Proguard shrinks unused code, optimizes bytecode, and obfuscates class names. When using Retrofit/Moshi, you must add @Keep or Proguard rules for DTOs so R8 doesn't strip or rename serialized fields in release builds!

quizzes.text: An app works fine in Debug mode, but crashes or fails to parse API JSON in the Release APK/AAB. What is the most likely culprit?
options: R8/Proguard obfuscated or stripped the API data model (DTO) classes
quizzes.explanation: In release builds with isMinifyEnabled = true, R8 renames fields unless protected by @Keep, @JsonClass(generateAdapter = true), or Proguard rules.
